message:
Expand the cycle from 12 to 16 days

Splits the Torso day apart and adds Knee, Neck, and Hips days. The old Torso
day was doing three unrelated jobs at once, and its two hip machines had no
real home there — they are single-joint hip isolation, not torso work.

Cycle changes:
- Torso dissolves into Transverse (rotation + anti-rotation) and Back (spinal
  extension); its Situps move to the Abs day
- New Knee day, defined by intent — slow eccentrics, isometric holds, tendon
  loading — so it does not become a second leg day. Leg Extension moves here
- New Neck day (retraction device, four-way isometrics)
- New Hips day covering all four hip actions, placed last so it primes the
  hips the day before Day 1 squats, mirroring how Pecs Mobility primes Push
- Ankle work joins the Calves day; Day 3 is renamed Stretching to match what
  it has always actually contained
- Compounds move to days 1 / 6 / 12, spaced 5-6-5 including the wrap. Grip
  now sits 8 days clear of Pulls and Bicep so forearm loading never stacks

Sessions run 1-3 exercises in practice regardless of how many a day lists, so
every day is now a short fixed list rather than a menu — spreading the same
coverage over more days keeps anything from being left out.

Code changes: cycle length is now derived from DAY_CONFIG rather than written
as a literal in five places. The cycle dial computes its own segment count,
ExercisesTab builds day filters from the config, the API bounds come from the
seeded day definitions, and the brand string tracks the day count.

message:
Identify days by slug and make cycle changes migrations

The cycle was addressed positionally in three places that could disagree — a
bundled DAY_CONFIG, a bundled DAY_DESIGN, and loose workout-day-definition
documents — so moving a day silently repointed every exercise and every logged
workout at whichever day took its slot. Changing it meant clicking an admin
button that deleted all the data and reinserted it from seed-data.js, with no
record of what ran or whether it finished.

Days now have a permanent slug. The number is only a day's position in one
version of the model, so reordering the cycle changes numbers and nothing else.

- The cycle is a `workout-model` document, one per generation, exactly one
  active. Retiring rather than deleting means a workout logged under Torso in
  2025 still resolves to Torso
- Logs record daySlug, dayNumber, dayName and modelVersion as they were on the
  day. Nothing later edits them — not a rename, not a reorder, not a new model
- dayDesign.js keys colors and anatomy by slug, retired days included, so
  history stops repainting itself when the cycle moves

Migrations replace the seed step. They are numbered, forward-only, ship in the
same image as the code that expects them, and run at pod startup before any
route is mounted; a failure exits the process and fails the rollout. Cosmos has
no cross-document transaction, so each one is written to survive being retried
from the top, and `npm run migrate:dry-run` checks exactly that by replaying
against the already-migrated result.

They auto-apply only in the cluster. Local development points at the live
database, so `npm run dev` reports what is pending rather than applying it —
otherwise starting a dev server on a branch would push a half-written migration
to production.

001 introduces the model and backfills slugs, changing no behaviour. 002 is the
12→16 expansion, which is now ordinary data rather than a schema rewrite.

Deletes seed-data.js, seed-soreness.js, seed-cardio-templates.js, the admin
route package, and the DatabaseInit panel. Day override survives as DayOverride,
the only control there that was ever a decision rather than a missing mechanism.

snapshot.db is regenerated in this commit because it is baked into the image;
left on the old schema, anonymous visitors would read a snapshot the new
frontend cannot parse until the 4-hourly cron caught up.

Also fixes the auto-advance wrap, which was a hardcoded 12 and would have
stranded the pointer on day 12 of 16, and the stale "Day 8 Shoulder Safety"
callout, which now reads its day numbers off the model.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge main, and carry soreness attribution onto day slugs

Main added soreness→workout attribution (#78) while this branch was moving day
identity off positional numbers, so the new feature arrived keyed the old way.

`sourceWorkoutDay` alone identified the day that caused the soreness, and the
recovery lanes coloured and named days from it. Entries now also carry
`sourceWorkoutDaySlug`; the number stays as the label the day had at the time,
which is the same rule logged workouts follow.

`DAY_MUSCLE_GROUPS` in sorenessLink.js was keyed by the old twelve numbers, so
it was already going to be wrong under a sixteen-day cycle regardless of this
branch — Day 5 would have offered pulling groups for the new Knee day. It is now
keyed by slug, covers all sixteen days, and keeps an entry for retired Torso.
Neck has no matching taxonomy group and deliberately falls through to the full
list rather than an empty one.

001 backfills the slug onto existing attributed entries.

Resolves the snapshot.db conflict by regenerating it, and drops admin-routes.js,
which main had edited and this branch deletes.
